label: A3 accessible occurrence transport strength and omission controls
paraphrase: Over unrestricted carriers: the accessible-occurrence transport law implies the earlier type-global-uniqueness law; UniqueRealization with admission read as occurrence at an accessible world, together with accessible occurrence of the selected occurrence, implies the relativized uniqueness hypothesis; and type-global selected uniqueness forces every bearer and every ordered start/finish pair to equal the selected occurrence's. In one finite Bool model two distinct occurrences share a transition and only one occurs: the relativized hypothesis and matching possible conditioning hold, type-global uniqueness fails, and the conclusion holds. Omitting the uniqueness hypothesis, or omitting the matching possible conditioning, makes the universal law false. Analyst controls only; no premise or root truth.
